task.title: crm_read/crm_write emitted a non-resolvable `supabase://` source reference
task.problem: 28 of 112 agents ran on the internal CRM tools and published `supabase://ivx_crm_prospects?prospect_type=...` as their evidence source reference. That scheme resolves nowhere, so the evidence was not independently verifiable and the senior gate correctly refused to count it.
task.rootCause: `sbRequest()` built the real HTTPS PostgREST URL internally but never returned it, so the CRM tools had nothing real to cite and invented a scheme instead.
task.fix: `SbResult` now carries the exact `sourceUrl` fetched; `crm_read` and `crm_write` publish that real HTTPS URL as their sourceReference.

findings: Credential leak check: Supabase PostgREST authenticates via `apikey` and `Authorization` HEADERS, never query parameters. The published URL therefore carries no secret. Asserted by an explicit test that fails if the service-role key, 'apikey', or 'authorization' appears in the sourceReference.
Host exposure: the URL embeds the Supabase project host, which is already public (EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL is a public client-side env var). No new exposure.
PII check on crm_write: the reference embeds `dedup_key`, which is `sha256(prospectType + normalized name).slice(0,40)` — a one-way hash, not raw prospect PII. Verified against makeDedupKey().
Row ids: crm_write may embed a CRM record UUID. That is an opaque internal identifier and the endpoint remains RLS/service-key protected; reading it requires credentials that are not in the URL.
sourceUrl is populated on BOTH the success and the catch path of sbRequest, so a failed request still reports what it attempted.
The missing-configuration early return intentionally omits sourceUrl — no URL was constructed, so none is claimed.

SbResult.sourceUrl is optional, so every existing SbResult construction site stays valid; the CRM tools keep their prior `supabase://` string as an explicit fallback rather than emitting an empty reference.
One template-string assignment per request, replacing an equivalent inline concatenation already present in the fetch call. No added I/O, allocation in a loop, or network round trip.
Measured: targeted suite 5 tests in 160ms; full backend suite 19.38s baseline vs 19.36s after — no measurable regression.
